title: Revision of the EU emissions trading system and the market stability reserve
date_evidence: 16 September 2026 (Members' Research Service briefing, Juan Fernando López Hernández)
key_claim: The Commission's 17 July 2026 proposal (COM(2026) 616) cuts the linear reduction factor from 4.4% to 3.7% in 2031-2035, lowers the MSR intake rate from 24% to 12% of allowances in circulation, lets MSR thresholds decline 4% a year from 2029, creates an Industrial Decarbonisation Bank with a EUR 100 billion envelope, and is targeted for agreement by the first quarter of 2027, against a net 90% EU emissions cut by 2040.
frame_summary: The Parliament's research service describes the Commission proposal as a package that aligns the ETS with the 2040 target while easing the cap path, the reserve and free allocation for industry.
verbatim_quote: an intake rate of 12 % of the total number of allowances in circulation (TNAC) (currently 24 %) applies.
verbatim_list: For these sectors, the proposal reduces the LRF from 4.4 % to 3.7 % in the period 2031-2035
The amended European Climate Law mandates a net 90 % reduction of EU GHG emissions by 2040 compared with 1990 levels.
a revision of the EU ETS Directive and of the MSR Decision by the first quarter of 2027
aiming for a total €100 billion envelope
providing 400 million allowances on a first-come, first-served basis
The MSR thresholds would decrease annually by 4 % starting in 2029

title: Market stability reserve: Council agrees targeted amendment for a resilient and predictable carbon market
key_claim: EU ambassadors agreed to suspend invalidation of market stability reserve allowances until the end of 2030, so allowances held above the current 400 million threshold are not cancelled, and to introduce a higher threshold of 800 million allowances from 1 January 2031; over 3 billion allowances have been removed since invalidation began; the Council aims to conclude talks with Parliament by the end of 2026.
frame_summary: The Council presents a stand-alone reserve amendment as a targeted fix that keeps the market predictable while pausing cancellation of surplus allowances.
verbatim_quote: temporarily suspend the invalidation of allowances until the end of 2030
verbatim_list: EU member states' ambassadors today decided to temporarily suspend the invalidation of allowances until the end of 2030.
a higher invalidation threshold of 800 million allowances will be introduced
over 3 billion allowances have been removed from the market
the Council aims to conclude negotiations on this file by the end of 2026

title: European Council conclusions, 15 and 16 October 2026 (EUCO 14/26)
key_claim: Leaders asked co-legislators to accelerate work on the Market Stability Reserve to limit sharp price swings, asked the Commission to update its assessment of all impacts of ETS2, and called for a well-functioning, transparent and predictable carbon market with less price volatility and a limited effect on electricity prices.
frame_summary: Leaders keep the ETS as the market-based carbon price signal but direct the reserve and the ETS2 design toward limiting price volatility and electricity-price impact.
verbatim_quote: a well-functioning, transparent and predictable carbon market
verbatim_list: accelerate the ongoing legislative process on the Market Stability Reserve
update the assessment of all impacts of ETS2

title: Position Paper September 2026: EU ETS amendments, what matters
key_claim: Sandbag calculates that the current total allowance surplus is 1.7 times 2025 ETS emissions and that the full Commission proposal, with no removals bought, would create a surplus of 4.4 times 2040 emissions (1,309 in its table); with the linear reduction factor at 3.7% throughout, 2.3 times, and at 3.7% then 2.7%, 3.3 times; it says such levels of surplus have never been reached, even when prices crashed to EUR 3 in 2013.
frame_summary: Sandbag argues the Commission and Parliament rapporteur proposals weaken ambition unnecessarily because CBAM already shields industry, and that the resulting surplus would undercut the long-term carbon price.
verbatim_quote: have never been reached in the EU ETS, even when the EUA price crashed to €3 in 2013

title: Out of balance: Assessing the 2026 Commission proposal for the EU ETS 1
key_claim: The Öko-Institut finds the proposal would create significant oversupply in 2031-2040: theoretical allowance supply of around 7,300 million EUAs against cumulative target-scenario emissions of around 5,400 MtCO2e, with the linear reduction factor change increasing the cap by 1,600 million EUAs (45%).
frame_summary: The Öko-Institut argues the Commission's supply-side changes would weaken the carbon-price signal and put the 2040 target at risk, and that the linear reduction factor should stay at 4.4% until at least 2035.
verbatim_quote: increase the cap by 1,600 million EUAs (45%)
verbatim_list: Overall, this results in a theoretical allowance supply of around 7,300 million EUAs during the fifth trading period.
cumulative emissions in the target scenario amount to only around 5,400 MtCO2e.

title: Carbon Market Strategist: EU ETS review signals less scarcity and more industrial policy
date_evidence: 24 August 2026, 17:30 pm (Moutaz Altaghlibi, Senior Economist, Energy Research)
key_claim: ABN AMRO forecasts allowance prices of 91 EUR/tCO2 in 2030 (May baseline 138) and 164 in 2035 (191), says the review reduces long-term scarcity while the 2040 target is unchanged, and expects a shift from carbon pricing toward a mix of carbon pricing, industrial policy and public support, with prices still elevated.
frame_summary: A bank research desk argues the review lowers long-run scarcity and the forecast carbon price while prices stay elevated, moving the system toward industrial policy.
verbatim_quote: The EU ETS review reduces long-term allowance scarcity while EU's climate targets remain unchanged.

title: An ETS that works for businesses and the climate: CLG Europe position on the ETS review
key_claim: CLG Europe, a business leadership group convened by the Cambridge Institute for Sustainability Leadership, says a strong and predictable carbon-price signal is essential for investment cases, warns that the combined supply changes risk recreating a surplus, and says companies that already invested should not be disadvantaged by reforms that lower the expected return.
frame_summary: A business coalition supports the ETS as the investment framework but asks that the package be stress-tested because cumulative supply changes could weaken the price signal investors relied on.
verbatim_quote: should not be disadvantaged by reforms that lower the expected return on those investments
verbatim_list: Maintaining a sufficiently strong and predictable carbon-price signal is essential

title: New EU compromise: major change to emissions allowances market
key_claim: Czech trade press reports that the Commission's proposal would stop cancelling allowances held above 400 million in the reserve, member states proposed no cancellation until 2030 and a threshold of 800 million from 2031 (per Reuters), and Parliament wants to keep cancellation with a threshold raised to 650 million allowances from 1 March 2027.
frame_summary: Czech trade press reports the reserve negotiation as a three-way contest over how high the cancellation threshold should be set, with Parliament seeking a lower one than the Council.
verbatim_quote: They want to retain the cancellation mechanism and only raise its threshold to 650 million allowances from 1 March 2027.
verbatim_list: However, the states today proposed an amendment under which allowances will not be cancelled until 2030.
notes: Fetched live via WebFetch 20/10/2026; sandbox audit egress blocked, quote confirmed by hand against the live page. Wire-based trade press; used to corroborate the Parliament position, which the article attributes to Parliament without naming a committee.
